records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: Personally designed and built an internal dispatch reconciliation tool to reconcile dispatch records and reduce repetitive reconciliation at the dispatch desk. It addressed mismatched references, not delivery route optimization. Operators compared an overnight spreadsheet against a daily export. The tool used a Python parser and SQL checks, with Git for version control and PostgreSQL as the production database. Supervisors sought understandable exceptions; a visible warning was preferred for late source files, and empty rows stayed visible. The tool supported operational use at the dispatch desk; no external product sales are stated.

decisions.reason: The name, role summary, and each negated professional experience are supported by the source.
The employer, title, dates, personal work, and training summary are supported. The training summary avoids asserting a disputed attendee count.

The project description, tools, scope, operational context, and personal versus team attributions are supported. The aliases are explicitly identified as names for the same project, and the summary does not claim the preferred warning was implemented or that the tool was sold externally.
The separate SQL checklist, Harbor Tools context, night-shift handover documentation, and absence of recorded user count or outcome are supported.

The time reduction, six-run measurement, three-hour weekly difference, team attribution, Ada's stated contribution, coworker behavior, and correction that delivery speed was not measured are supported.
The record accurately reports that the source gives conflicting attendance counts—12 in the initial account and 14 on a later sheet—and says the discrepancy cannot be resolved.

The documentation claim is supported, but the SQL skill link is not established for the documentation work itself; the source identifies Roster Note as a SQL checklist but does not say SQL was used to document its handover.
The source explicitly says Ada wrote the Python parser herself for Dispatch Loom.
The source supports personal SQL work on Dispatch Loom and Roster Note and explicitly says SQL was used extensively.
The source explicitly states PostgreSQL was used for the production database.
The source explicitly states Git was used for version control, and the Collaboration category is given in the source.
The record accurately preserves the conflicting workshop attendance counts of 12 and 14 and the source's statement that the discrepancy cannot be resolved.
